text:
jen: Quick check — need to give a contractor read access to prod logs for a one-off PII-redaction QA. Want least-privilege and short duration. Any preferred approach?
omar: How long do they need it and which project/org?
jen: 4 hours. Project = redwood-prod-analytics (project id: redwood-prod-analytics). They only need to view logs, not export. Logs include IPs and user IDs — goal is to avoid exposing raw PII if possible.
kai: IAM won't redact. Options: pre-redact via export/sink or create a view that excludes message payloads. If neither is possible quickly, ephemeral console access + strict monitoring is the pragmatic path.
omar: Agreed. Two quick paths: (A) create a redacted BigQuery export and grant bq.dataViewer, or (B) temporary roles/logging.viewer + monitoring and session recording. Which is faster?
jen: We don't have a pre-redacted export. For a 4h job, (B) is quicker. Security — ok with temporary raw view if we add controls? @sec-bot?
sec-bot: Automated policy check: project redwood-prod-analytics contains flagged PII logs. Recommend against direct raw access unless logs are pre-redacted. If granted, require: ticket ID + justification, owner present, session recording, IP restriction, and expiry <= 4h.
omar: Technically we can issue a conditional binding with an expression that limits by principal and time. That covers expiry. We should also require contractor to be on corp VPN IP range.
kai: Note — removing specific logging permissions often breaks the UI. I suggest roles/logging.viewer with a condition and strict audit. Example condition: request.auth.principal == "user:contractor@thirdco.com" && request.time < timestamp('2026-03-18T02:00:00Z').
omar: Example gcloud command to add a conditional binding (adjust timestamps):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod-analytics \
  --member='user:contractor@thirdco.com' \
  --role='roles/logging.viewer' \
  --condition='title=tmp_jen,expression=request.auth.principal=="user:contractor@thirdco.com" && request.time<timestamp("2026-03-18T02:00:00Z"),description=4h temp access'
```
kai: Also restrict to contractor VPN net: add && request.ip == '203.0.113.0/24' or similar if provider supports. Otherwise enforce VPN and record allowed IPs in the ticket.
sec-bot: Approval checklist: ticket ID, owner, justification, session recording requirement, allowed IPs, expiry timestamp. Post ticket link and I will mark approval if everything matches.
jen: Created ticket INC-4321: https://tickets.redwood.internal/INC-4321 — owner @jen. Contractor email contractor@thirdco.com. Allowed IPs: 203.0.113.0/24 (contractor VPN). Expires 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z. I will run the conditional binding now. Approve?
alex: SRE ok from my side. Add alerting: IAM change, data access anomaly, and page me + @omar on suspicious access.
sec-bot: Temporary approval pending execution. Ensure session recording link is attached and audit logs retention is enabled for this project. :white_check_mark:
jen: Executing now — using our /tools/jit-grant wrapper to create the conditional binding and enable recording. Will paste resulting policy snippet once done.
jen: Done — policy binding added. Snippet:
```
- role: roles/logging.viewer
  members:
  - user:contractor@thirdco.com
  condition:
    title: tmp_jen
    expression: request.auth.principal=="user:contractor@thirdco.com" && request.time<timestamp("2026-03-18T02:00:00Z")
    description: 4h temp access
```
jen: Session recording link: https://session-archive.redwood/internal/rec/abcd1234 — audit alerts created and owners paged. Closing after contractor confirms access and completes tasks.
sec-bot: Marking approved and monitoring enabled. Reminder: rotate or remove any creds touched and confirm access revoked after expiry.
jen: Contractor confirmed via DM they can access what they need and will not export data. I'll follow up with a short postmortem entry once complete. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
